# MDL407 · `octal-integer`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

An integer written with a leading 0 is read in octal.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | options |
| Default severity | warning |
| Fix | — |
| Design references | G7 |
| Proven on real mydumper by | [`mdl407-octal-threads`](../../e2e/scenarios/mdl407-octal-threads.txtar) |

## Why

GLib parses integer options with C's `strtol` in base 0: a leading `0` means octal. `threads=010` sets 8 threads, not 10. Write the number without the leading zero, or keep it if octal is really meant (no fix: both readings are plausible).

## Example

With mydumper v0.19.3-3:

❌ Before:

```ini
[mydumper]
threads=010
```

```text
2:9-2:12 warning MDL407[octal-integer] `010` is octal: `threads` gets 8, not 10
  = threads uses 8.
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL407: warning   # or error, info, off
```

To accept one occurrence, put `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=MDL407` on the line above it.
